completed.title: Root cause: NDEController.all_checks_off silently broke TraCI lane changes
completed.detail: User reported AV still getting stuck in lane 0 behind the stalled car at 4411907471#0_0 pos 312, despite previous bypass logic firing 307 times per stall-edge traversal. Traced through SUMO LaneChangeMode bit semantics and found that NDEController.all_checks_off() unconditionally calls setLaneChangeMode(veh_id, 0) before processing LEFT/RIGHT commands — mode=0 disables both autonomous LC AND TraCI LC requests, so every changeLaneRelative call was silently dropped by SUMO. Fixed in execute_lane_change_command(): explicitly call setLaneChangeMode(veh_id, 256) right before changeLaneRelative so TraCI requests are respected. After the fix, AV enters stall edge in lane 1 at 14.5 m/s, traverses 96 of 113 ticks in lane 1, exits via 4126471851#0 lane 1, and continues route — instead of staying stuck at speed 0 for the entire run.

completed.title: Built a CNDE↔NADE-adversity trajectory-conflict logger (design + module + integration)
completed.detail: When CNDE is enabled, both the MotionTransformer NN and the adversity manager can issue commands for the same BV in the same tick; the merge function at packages/terasim-nde-nade/terasim_nde_nade/envs/nade.py:308 silently keeps NADE's command and drops CNDE's whenever NADE is not DEFAULT, with no record of what was discarded. New module packages/terasim-nde-nade/terasim_nde_nade/utils/trajectory_conflict_logger.py installs a per-tick observer at that exact merge point. It emits one JSONL record per veh_id with fields {sim_time, tick, veh_id, in_nade, in_cnde, nade_cmd_type, nade_adversity_class, cnde_first_point, sumo_current, cnde_sumo_offset_m, resolution} and resolutions ∈ {cnde_won, nade_won_adversarial, cnde_dropped_membership, nade_only, default_only}. Lazy file open + flush-on-every-write means it's crash-safe; entirely env-var gated (TRAJECTORY_CONFLICT_LOG=1) so existing runs are byte-identical when disabled. Full design at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-18-cnde-adversity-trajectory-conflict-logging-design.md. First CNDE-on run (sim8) produced 19,368 records and showed dyn_bv_20 toggling between cnde_won and FollowerAdversity for >50s before the run crashed — exactly the silent-drop pattern the logger was built to catch.

completed.title: Root-caused why AV bypass LC was silently rejected, fixed via SUMO TraciLaneChangePriority bits
completed.detail: AV would issue LEFT/RIGHT every tick when blocked by a static-adversity stalled object 311m → 28m ahead, but the lane index never changed; AV crawled into the obstacle. Reading /home/haotian/.terasim/deps/sumo/src/microsim/MSVehicle.cpp Influencer::setLaneChangeMode and the TraciLaneChangePriority enum in MSVehicle.h: bits 8–9 of laneChangeMode encode the priority; the code constant _LC_MODE_BYPASS = 256 (bits 8–9 = 01) is LCP_NOOVERLAP — TraCI LC silently rejected whenever any neighbor overlaps AV's body in the target lane. The in-tree comment claimed it was 'TraCI commands respected' but that's only true with a clear gap. Changed envs/nade_with_av.py:1107 _LC_MODE_BYPASS = 0 (LCP_ALWAYS — change regardless of blockers, SUMO adapts blocker speeds) and vehicle/nde_controller.py:621 mode_value = 0 if veh_id == AV else 256 (BVs keep 256 for adversarial maneuver safety). End-to-end verification (sim7): AV depart=10.1s arrive=3851.9s routeLength=21,490.93m rerouteNo=0 finish_reason=AV_left — the full predefined NCRC route, no detours, with 5658 av_bypass_fire events and 1327 lc_fire + 9037 leader_fire + 1104 follower_fire + 176 tfl_fire.

completed.title: Fixed body-overlap check for AV's reactive force-moveTo teleport (replaced naive behind-only filter)
completed.detail: The reactive bypass path force-teleports AV laterally when it's stopped < 0.1 m/s and within 15m of a slow leader. Previous safety filter at envs/nade_with_av.py:~1210 only rejected the teleport when 'a vehicle is 0–10m BEHIND AV in the target lane'; a vehicle whose front sat at av_pos with its body extending backwards was missed entirely. In sim 'sim5' AV teleported onto dyn_bv_34 at lane 4117050240_3 → next libsumo.executeMove segfaulted. Replaced with a precise body-interval intersection test: tgt_body = [av_pos + 1 − av_len, av_pos + 1]; for each neighbor v on the target lane, compute v_body = [v_front − v_len, v_front] and reject if the intervals overlap with a 0.5 m clearance margin. Uses real getLength() per neighbor instead of a blanket 15m window so it doesn't over-reject. Adds an INFO log on rejection with the exact intervals so future debug is easier. Verified in sim6 — 90+ rejections fired across one run, no executeMove segfault from this path.

completed.title: Junction-lane guards at four call sites — adversity_manager, leader_adversity, controller, AV bypass
completed.detail: Calling traci.vehicle.* on a vehicle whose current lane id starts with ':' (an internal junction lane) corrupts SUMO's internal data structures in libsumo (in-process, no boundary check) and the corruption surfaces as a SIGSEGV on the next executeMove. Added consistent guards: (1) utils/adversity/adversity_manager.py:derive_command — bail out early with a no-op DEFAULT command when ego is on an internal lane OR missing from traci.vehicle.getIDList(); (2) utils/adversity/leader_adversity.py:derive_leader_adversarial_command — same checks plus a try/except around traci.vehicle.getLeader (which itself can segfault on a fragile vehicle); (3) vehicle/nde_controller.py:execute_trajectory_command — skip ALL trajectory control while the vehicle is on an internal lane, BEFORE setSpeedMode/setLaneChangeMode are called (these were running first under the old code and likely contributed to the corruption); (4) envs/nade_with_av.py:predict_av_control_command — top-of-function bail when AV itself is on an internal lane. Each guard eliminated a distinct crash signature observed in sim11–14.

completed.title: Tried + reverted a DTM route-aware BV spawn fix (would-be issue 3)
completed.detail: User reported BVs occasionally make abrupt lane-changes 'at the finish line' — e.g. a BV travels straight in a lane then sweeps left right before a junction. Confirmed mechanism: DTM's ahead-spawn branches at packages/terasim-nde-nade/terasim_nde_nade/utils/dynamic_traffic_manager.py:467,503 pick t_lane = random.randint(0, n_lanes-1); BVs inherit AV's route from spawn_edge onwards (lcStrategic=10 boost at spawn). On edges where only specific lanes connect to the next route edge (e.g. 4117050240 has 4 lanes but only lane 3 → 4126464931#0), BVs spawned on a non-compatible lane must do an aggressive last-second strategic LC near the junction, which from a top-down view looks like a left turn. Implemented a helper _route_compatible_lanes() that filters spawn lanes via traci.lane.getLinks against the route's next edge. Worked as advertised — but sim10 showed AV got stuck on edge 4411907471#0 for 178s and SUMO triggered a rerouter (rerouteNo=1, routeLength dropped 21.5km → 3.6km). The denser route-correct BV distribution starved AV's lane of throughput. Reverted the DTM patch; documented as 'same strategic-LC mechanism as AV's own behaviour on this map — not a bug, the map's lane connectivity is the cause'.

in_progress.title: ASAN-instrumented libsumo run against NCRC — catching the libsumo executeMove segfault at the C level
in_progress.detail: Built a -fsanitize=address debug version of libsumo into /home/haotian/.terasim/sumo-asan-build/ (separate from the pip-installed conda env libsumo at /home/haotian/miniconda3/envs/terasim/lib/python3.10/site-packages/libsumo/, which is untouched). Output _libsumo.so verified to have 782 asan symbols + libasan.so.8 in its ldd. Running NCRC under it with `PYTHONPATH=/home/haotian/.terasim/deps/sumo/tools LD_PRELOAD=libasan.so.8 ASAN_OPTIONS='halt_on_error=1:detect_leaks=0:malloc_context_size=30' python scripts/run_experiment_cnde.py …`. ASAN slowdown is steep (~100× sim-time vs real-time observed — much worse than the 3-10× textbook number); after 1h elapsed AV is at sim_time ~117s, vs the historical crash window of ~300–450s, so ETA to the crash is several more hours. When SIGSEGV hits, ASAN will print the heap-use-after-free / out-of-bounds-write trace with three back-stacks (current access, free, alloc) — that's the precise root cause we've been chasing. Waiter (bt367g1hm) + monitor (b29bl5na2) armed to notify on exit.

in_progress.title: Parallel printf-instrumented libsumo subagent — faster path to the bad TraCI call
in_progress.detail: Dispatched a parallel subagent to build a RelWithDebInfo (no ASAN) libsumo into ~/.terasim/sumo-debug-build/ with fprintf(stderr, '[TRACI] t=… fn=… veh=… edge=… lane=… pos=…') at the entry of every suspect TraCI write — moveToXY, moveTo, setSpeed, setSpeedMode, setLaneChangeMode, changeLane, changeLaneRelative, remove — plus [STEP] executeMove_start/_end markers in MSEdgeControl. Each fprintf wrapped in try/catch since the underlying state-fetch (getRoadID/getLaneID) is itself fragile on junction lanes and must never raise out of the instrumentation. Build ETA 5-10 min, sim ETA 3-15 min at normal speed. The last [TRACI] line before the segfault tells us which call corrupted state; an [STEP] executeMove_start with no matching _end tells us the corruption was already there before the C-level step started. Runs entirely in parallel; both approaches will land independently and INC-164 will get the findings from whichever fires first.

todo.title: Apply the C-level fix once ASAN/printf identifies the corruption site
todo.detail: All of today's Python-side guards (junction guards at four call sites, body-overlap teleport check, existence checks, LC-mode correction) eliminate specific crash modes but the next deeper one keeps surfacing because libsumo (in-process) gives TraCI writes direct access to SUMO internals — there's no boundary between Python and SUMO's C++ data structures. The right fix is a libsumo Vehicle.cpp pre-check at the entry of position/control writes that refuses to operate on vehicles in fragile states (internal lane, mid-removal, mid-collision) and returns a TraCIException to Python rather than corrupting state. Once ASAN or the printf trace localizes the exact entry function, decide whether to upstream a SUMO patch or maintain a local libsumo fork.

completed.title: Made AV bypass route-aware so it picks the lane that actually connects to AV's next required route edge, instead of mechanical +1/-1
completed.detail: packages/terasim-nde-nade/terasim_nde_nade/envs/nade_with_av.py predict_av_control_command: replaced the heuristic 'target_lane = av_lane_idx + 1 if room else -1' with a getLinks-based picker. For each non-obstacle lane on AV's current edge, query traci.lane.getLinks(<edge>_<li>) and check if any outgoing link's next-lane belongs to next_edge_id = av_route[av_route_idx + 1]. Among the lanes that do connect, pick the one closest to AV's current lane. When the picker runs but finds no off-obstacle valid lane (i.e. obstacle is in the only lane that connects to next required edge), abort bypass entirely — set target_delta = 0 so AV queues in current lane rather than being pushed off-route by the dumb fallback. Earlier off-route incident on edge 4117050240 — dyn_bv_6 was sitting on lane 3 (the only lane connecting to 4126464931#0), the bypass excluded lane 3 then fell back to +1 and pushed AV onto lane 2, which only connects to off-route 1421787431#0. The new abort branch eliminates that pattern.

completed.title: Made AV bypass only fire on real stalled adversity objects, not slow BVs or red-light queues
completed.detail: Added a stalled-only filter at the top of the bypass-leader resolution: 'if bypass_leader is not None and not _is_adv_obj(bypass_leader[0]): bypass_leader = None'. _is_adv_obj returns True for ID containing _stalled_object / _CONE_ / _collision — these are the StalledObjectAdversity-spawned vehicles and construction cones. For anything else (dyn_bv_*, normal traffic stopped at red light, queuing BVs near intersections), AV now uses SUMO's IDM car-following and queues normally. Previously the reactive branch (AV.speed < 2 m/s AND leader.speed < 2 m/s AND dist < 15 m) was over-triggering on any slow vehicle, causing AV to attempt LC into adjacent lanes whenever it queued — that's the left↔right ping-pong the user observed.

completed.title: Replaced force-moveTo teleport with native traci.vehicle.changeLane(AV, target, 3.0s) — smooth interpolated lateral LC
completed.detail: Previously the bypass used traci.vehicle.moveTo(AV, target_lane_id, pos) which instantly teleports AV across lane boundaries — visually disturbing in GUI mode and the source of the libsumo executeMove segfault when target lane had a body-overlap blocker (INC-164). Switched to traci.vehicle.changeLane(AV, target_lane, LATERAL_LC_DURATION) which interpolates the lateral position over 3 seconds — SUMO's normal LC physics, visible as a smooth move in sumo-gui. Together with setLaneChangeMode(AV, 0=LCP_ALWAYS) the LC fires regardless of safety, and SUMO adapts blocker speeds to make room rather than rejecting. Critical bug fix on top of this: the setLaneChangeMode call was running AFTER changeLane in the same tick, so changeLane was using the previous tick's default mode 1621 (LCP_NOOVERLAP) which silently rejects whenever a body-overlap exists in the target lane. Diag confirmed AV firing changeLane 30 times in 60s on hotspot 1 with no actual lane change. Moved the setLaneChangeMode call to immediately before changeLane — now LCP_ALWAYS is in effect when the LC command is interpreted.

completed.title: Added 3-second post-LC cooldown to prevent AV from ping-ponging left↔right between adjacent lanes
completed.detail: Added self._bypass_cooldown_until attribute. After every successful changeLane, set cooldown = sim_time + 3.0s. The bypass trigger condition is gated by 'not in_cooldown' — during the 3-second window after a LC, no new bypass command is issued no matter what the bypass leader / cross-lane state looks like. This eliminates the failure mode where bypass picker oscillates because both lanes have intermittent slow leaders: tick N picks lane 1, tick N+1 picker finds new leader in lane 1 and picks lane 0, tick N+2 etc.

completed.title: Added per-edge AV_cfg.lane_preferences in YAML — pin AV to a preferred lane upon entering specific edges, before reaching obstacles
completed.detail: configs/simulation/ncrc_combined_adversity.yaml AV_cfg now accepts a lane_preferences mapping of {edge_id: lane_idx}. NADEWithAV.__init__ reads it into self._lane_prefs. The new enforcement block at the top of predict_av_control_command (after the junction-internal-lane guard but before all reactive bypass logic) checks if AV's current edge is in the preferences table; if AV is not yet on the preferred lane, calls setLaneChangeMode(AV, 0) and changeLane(AV, pref_lane, 5.0) with a 3-second cooldown to avoid spam. For the NCRC scenario: 4411907471#0 → 1 (stalled_car on lane 0 pos 312) and 4126464941#0 → 1 (two stalled trucks on lane 0). AV is force-LCed to lane 1 the instant it enters either edge, hundreds of meters before the obstacle, instead of relying on last-second reactive bypass that fails in dense traffic. The secondary benefit: SUMO no longer speculatively reroutes AV at the junction (because lane-0 → next-route-edge being blocked is not a problem when AV is already in lane 1), so the GUI's 'show future route' visualization stays clean.

completed.title: Diagnosed the av_route_mutated GUI display issue and confirmed AV physically stays on the predefined route despite the visualization glitch
completed.detail: User saw the GUI's future-route highlight showing a wrong (off-route) detour at the first stalled vehicle's junction. Initial hypothesis was that SUMO's auto-rerouting device was permanently mutating AV's route. So the mutation events are SUMO's speculative reroute computed when AV is in lane 0 with the lane-0 → next-route-edge internal connection blocked by yaml's block_internal_lanes — the auto-reroute is recomputed each tick and reverts as soon as AV LCes to lane 1. The lane_preferences fix above eliminates this entirely by keeping AV in lane 1 from edge entry.

completed.detail: After the leak fix, observed env_step times of 5.5 s while adversity_ms was only 25 ms — the bulk was elsewhere. Added per-sub-call instrumentation in nade.py NADE_decision that writes a record to nade_decision_timing.jsonl whenever total > 500 ms (one perf_counter pair, near-zero overhead). The data attributes 99.99 % of slow steps to predict_environment_future_trajectory (nade.py:447 → trajectory_predictor.py:583). Pattern in the data is unmistakable exponential doubling: sim_t 1318.4=680 ms → 1318.9=1291 → 1319.1=2704 → 1319.6=5587 → plateau ~5500 ms for 13 sim-s → reset to 700 ms for 7 sim-s → next doubling rises past the original plateau to 22 s, then in user's longer run all the way to 368 s/step at sim_t 1405. The 'reset' behaviour shows the regime is state-driven not algorithmic O(N²). Source code already references INC-143 by name in a comment at nade.py:441, so this is a re-occurrence of a known issue.

completed.title: Located the likely state amplification path — CNDE TRAJECTORY commands in 'continuing' mode feeding ever-longer future_trajectory arrays into NADE re-interpolation

Hypothesis: CNDE itself emits progressively longer trajectories when adversarial-trajectory mode is sticky on a dataset BV, and NADE re-interpolation of those long arrays at 0.5 s resolution makes interp1d's source-points × target-points cost dominate.

completed.title: Root-caused INC-143 to NDEController.all_checks_on's findRoute+setRoute pair — full NCRC route now completes end-to-end under both seed=42 and seed=1000
completed.detail: Spent the day chasing the 2^N route-doubling pattern that capped sim progression at sim_t ~850-1525 across 12 attempts. Each Python-side defense (route_length_list cache, raw-route cache, slice truncation, degenerate-route quarantine, traci.route.add + setRouteID replacement) bought another few hundred sim-s before SUMO's internal route storage ballooned again. Final breakthrough was instrumenting every route-mutating traci API via a monkey-patch in utils/agents/vehicle.py with ROUTE_TRACE=1 env var, dumping per-call caller stacks to /tmp/route_trace.jsonl. In ~5 min of sim, dyn_bv_5 alone got 76 setRoute calls — all traced back to nde_controller.py:746 (now :736) inside all_checks_on, which fires every CNDE release cycle and does traci.simulation.findRoute(current, dest) followed by traci.vehicle.setRoute(veh_id, route_stage.edges). The interaction between SUMO's setRoute and findRoute on a mid-route vehicle is what feeds the perfect 2^N doubling, up to 2^26 = 67M edges per BV before SUMO's own step() hangs in C++ for 12+ minutes.

SUMO continues with the existing route fine, and DTM despawns the BV on distance when it leaves the AV vicinity. Tested both seeds: seed=42 ran 3167 sim_t / 31528 steps with 13847 adversity fires, av_final_edge = 4117050250 (the last edge of the configured route). Seed=1000 ran 3401 sim_t / 33864 steps with 12903 fires, same final edge. RSS stayed flat at ~5.7 GB for the entire run in both cases vs the baseline OOM at 80 GB.

Plus _RAW_ROUTE_CACHE per veh_id that only refetches traci.vehicle.getRoute() once the vehicle has advanced past a forward window — avoids the ~1s libsumo→Python marshal when SUMO's stored route is large from pre-fix simulations. Also added a forward-only slice of veh_info.route to [idx-1, idx+30] so all downstream operations are bounded regardless of SUMO's storage size. Together with the all_checks_on guard, predict_future_ms now stays well under 200ms throughout a full NCRC route, vs the 5.5s → 24s → 368s doubling plateau seen before any of the fixes.

completed.detail: Earlier in the day we'd documented INC-164 as 'partially fixed' — UB#1 (MSLaneChanger bool init) and UB#2 (MSLink null guard) were already patched in the deployed libsumo binary (md5 5c493e28), but ~20 % of seeds still segfaulted inside libsumo executeMove. Today after a forced PC reboot for the GPU driver mismatch (more on that below), spent some time on Track 4 of the multi-track investigation: fetched SUMO upstream/main (716 commits past v1_23_1, plus a fresh v1_27_0 release), filtered for `crash|segfault|null|sanit|ubsan|undefined|uninit` keywords, and got two candidates. `fa6f211cd5d` 'fixed uninitialized value. refs #2380' (Jakob Erdmann, 2026-04-09) was an exact match for our UB#1 pattern — a single-line constructor init-list addition `myDontBrake(false),` in MSLCM_LC2013 (Lane Change Model 2013). The field was being read at line 322 `if (gotOne && !myDontBrake)` before any of the conditional assignment paths (lines 1031, 1075, 1090) had a chance to set it, giving random behavior on uninit memory. Cherry-picked the patch into ~/.terasim/deps/sumo/src/microsim/lcmodels/MSLCM_LC2013.cpp, rebuilt libsumo in sumo-build-gui (Release with FOX/GUI), got new binary md5 871ab7aa99b317dcfcb7802ecb06593c (26 MB), deployed to the terasim env. Verified end-to-end: 4-seed batch (7, 42, 100, 314) — seed=42 reliably segfaulted at sim_t 900.2 before the fix; now reaches av_final_edge=4117050250 at sim_t 3363. Seeds 7 and 100 also completed (3079, 3074). seed=314 hit CUDA OOM at sim_t 1957 from 4-parallel GPU contention, unrelated to UB#3.

completed.title: GPU driver/library mismatch broke all CUDA after the morning batch — root-caused to nvidia-driver-580 package half-installed (DKMS .ko not built), gcc-12 was needed, and rebuilt .ko was Secure-Boot-rejected; fixed by disabling Secure Boot in MSI BIOS
completed.detail: After the morning's first 5-parallel batch hit CUDA OOM on seed=666, NVML stopped initializing — `Failed to initialize NVML: Driver/library version mismatch, NVML library version: 580.159`. Kernel had 580.142 loaded, userspace was 580.159. Root cause: `nvidia-driver-580` had been apt-upgraded but DKMS had only `added` (not `built`) the .ko module. `sudo dpkg --configure -a` triggered a DKMS build that failed with `cc: error: unrecognized command-line option -ftrivial-auto-var-init=zero` — Ubuntu 22.04's default gcc-11 doesn't know that flag (kernel 6.8 HWE was built with gcc-12). Installed gcc-12, retried, build now succeeded. Reboot → still `couldn't communicate with the NVIDIA driver`, and `modprobe nvidia` failed with `Key was rejected by service` — UEFI Secure Boot wouldn't load the unsigned DKMS-built module. Three resolution paths existed (disable SB in BIOS, enroll a MOK key, or use Ubuntu's pre-signed `linux-modules-nvidia-580-$(uname -r)`). User went with the simplest — into MSI PRO B760-VC WIFI BIOS (Del to enter, F7 → Advanced Mode → Settings → Advanced → Windows OS Configuration → Secure Boot Disabled), and rebooted. CUDA + libsumo back online.

Expectation: SUMO's route equals that_path. Observed: route equals the_path concatenated with prior route, doubling on repeated calls. completed.title: 读 Behavioral Safety Assessment 论文 (Liu et al., arXiv 2505.16214v2)：梳理 DLT+DIT 框架及 Autoware.Universe 3e-3/mile crash rate 结果
completed.detail: 通读 25 页论文，核心是把 AV 评估范式从 functional safety（车辆中心，ISO 26262/21448/PAS 8800）转向 behavioral safety（环境中心，评估 AV 与交通环境的反应+交互行为）。框架含两个互补组件：Driver Licensing Test (DLT) 用 14 个代表性场景（cut-in、car-following、lane departure、左右转、VRU 穿行、roundabout、vehicle encroachment、traffic signal，覆盖城市 ODD 71.5% 撞车类型），每场景按碰撞所需减速度分 5 个 risk level，评估反应行为；Driving Intelligence Test (DIT) 在 Mcity 仿真完整 trip，基于自研 TeraSim 构造 NDE，再用 NADE（importance sampling，ε=3000）放大 rare event，输出统计 crash rate。关键结果：Autoware.Universe DLT 通过 6/14；DIT crash rate 3.01e-3 crashes/mile，约人类（3.00e-6）的 1000 倍；crash 类型 rear-end 72.9% / angle 22% / sideswipe 2.7% / head-on 2.4%；NDE crash rate 仿真 2.93e-6 对齐 Michigan 真实 3.00e-6（高保真）。发现 3 类系统性问题：obstacle-avoidance replanning bug（已反馈修复）、right-of-way 不主动让行、trajectory prediction 未用红绿灯信息。代码/数据开源在 zenodo 15446750 / 15446739。与 ISUZU accident-rate investigation 直接相关：DIT 的 TeraSim+NADE+14 场景 DLT 是可直接借鉴的 benchmark 方法。

completed.title: 核对 TeraSim ISUZU 分支当前 accident-rate 算法，并确认 monitor.json 的 weight 就是论文 importance-sampling likelihood ratio
completed.detail: 梳理两套并存的 accident-rate 范式。新路径：run_experiment_cnde.py 的 _print_run_summary() 每次仿真结束写 accident_summary.{json,txt}，含 conditional rate（per class = av_crashes_attributed/fires，在 probability 变化下不变，描述该 adversity 类的本质危险度）+ absolute rate（per run = av_collisions/sim_duration_s 或 /km，随 probability 线性缩放）；归因用 5 秒 lookback（每次 AV 碰撞往回找对方 BV 最近一次 *_fire 事件，归到对应 class，未命中进 no_attribution，实测 <5%）；触发改成每个 adversity class 独立的 Bernoulli probability 门控（在 trigger() 里抽样），替代已废弃的全局 adversity_sampling_probability。建立这套算法的核心 commit 是 3f87efe / c761ce2 / 49da60f / e282b4a / 54e537d。老路径：nade.py 的 on_stop() 把 self.record 写成 monitor.json，顶层 weight 字段 = 整轮 importance-sampling 累积权重，由 nade.py:683-700 的 weight *= ndd_adversarial_prob/IS_prob（或 normal 分支 ndd_normal_prob/(1-IS_prob)）逐步乘出，正是论文 Eq. W_q(x)=Π P(u|s)/q(u|s) 的 likelihood ratio；论文 unbiased 估计 P(A)=E[1{crash}·W_q] 用的就是这条路径。结论：两套范式不同——montior.json 是 IS 加权的无偏估计（对应论文），accident_summary 是观测频率（有偏，反映配置的 probability 混合）。

completed.title: 推翻早先『IDM 路口 T-bone 无敌』的判断：加 TERASIM_TRAFFIC_SCALE env 旋钮，用 traffic_scale=3 测试发现 TLS 真的能撞 AV（2/31 commits = 6.5% 转化率，vs traffic_scale=1 时 0/62）
completed.detail: 之前在 main canonical NADE 跑下看到 TLS 大量触发(62 次)但 0 撞车，我下结论是『SUMO IDM 路口主动让行 → T-bone 几乎不可能』。haotian 怀疑可能是横流不足而非 IDM 本质。验证方法：场景 ncrc_combined_adversity.yaml 用 aa_with_types.rou.xml（自然 Ann Arbor 流量）+ roundabout_traffic.add.xml（只给环岛加横流），信号路口没有专门加横流。给并行脚本加 TERASIM_TRAFFIC_SCALE 旋钮（注入 environment.parameters.traffic_scale），test scale=3 → TLS 提交 31 次（per-run 频率类似但绝对数因 n=8 较少）、AV 撞车 2 次中归因到 TLS 的 2 次 → IDM 让行只能挡掉 ~93%，剩下 ~7% 是无法躲的（多车同时冲突、最后一刻闯入等）。还揭示一个有意思的点：TLS 因为自然率 p 高(1e-2)、q 被 5% cap 截断 → 每次 TLS 撞车权重 = p/q = 0.2 远大于 leader 的 ~3e-3 → 即便 TLS 撞车数少，加权后 rate 贡献(5.4e-3)反而超过 leader(1.1e-3) → TLS 在加密横流下是 rate 主导项。

completed.title: 写了 traci 驱动的 SUMO replay 工具——之前以为 sumo-gui 有 --fcd-input，发现是错的，转用 moveToXY 重做
completed.detail: 客户问能不能看 simulation 回放。第一反应是写 FCD 转换器（heading_tracker.jsonl → FCD XML），写完才发现 sumo-gui 没有 --fcd-input 选项（只有 --fcd-output）——一个错误假设浪费了 10 分钟。改用 traci 子进程模式：起 sumo-gui，加 dummy route 让 vehicle.add 能工作，每 tick 用 moveToXY(keepRoute=2) 把车摆到 heading_tracker.jsonl 记录的 (x, y, angle) 位置，setSpeedMode(0)+setLaneChangeMode(0) 关掉 SUMO 物理避免轨迹被 IDM 改写。脚本 scripts/replay_in_sumo_gui.py（~100 行）。在 ub4_hunt_r29_s34021（NCRC 7109 ticks，sim_t 15→725s）上跑通，sumo-gui 窗口实际打开在 DISPLAY=:1，xdotool 确认到 window ID。回放限制：heading_tracker 只记 AV 100m 半径内的车，远处 BV 不会出现——客户能看到 AV + 周围 BV 行为，但看不到整张图。

completed.title: 把 visual replay 包成 sim-replay skill——客户说 'replay the last run' 就自动跑，仿 libsumo-rebuild 格式
completed.detail: 写了 .claude/skills/sim-replay/SKILL.md（~250 行）。description 字段设了一堆触发短语（'replay me the most recent sumo replay'、'show me the last run'、'play back that simulation'、'I want to see the AV trajectory'），让 Claude 主会话基于自然语言自动调起来。流程 5 步：(1) find output -name heading_tracker.jsonl -printf '%T@ %p' | sort -nr | head 自动挑最新 run dir；(2) 从 run_metadata.json 读 input_files.sumo_net 路径（fallback NCRC 默认 aa_fixed_enhanced.net.xml）；(3) DISPLAY=:1 xdpyinfo 验证 X server 可达；(4) nohup 后台启动 scripts/replay_in_sumo_gui.py；(5) xdotool search --name SUMO 验证窗口起来。带 troubleshooting 表（之前踩的 6 个坑都写进去：sumo-gui not found、fcd-input 不存在、Connection closed by SUMO 等）和无 X server 时的 matplotlib MP4 备用方案。

completed.title: Serial hunt 9h 31 runs / 0 crash 后怀疑 CNDE 没真跑——grep 验证：CNDE active 但控制 0 车辆 ~93% 时间
completed.detail: 客户问 'still didnt find it? you sure you are running cnde?'。查 r19（1578s 全程 run）的 loguru：'CNDE simulator built and configured' + 'CNDE Experiment started' + cnde_audit.jsonl 3.1 MB + cnde_trajectory_log.jsonl 18 MB——CNDE 确实在运行。但 grep 'Control commands: N CNDE' 分布: 30636 次 0 CNDE / 1738 次 1 / 514 次 2 / 198 次 3——只有 7.4% 的 tick 有 CNDE 控制。原因：cache_radius=100m, control_radius=50m，但 NCRC 路线大段时间 AV 周围没 BV 进 control_radius（log 显示 cache=1 即只有 AV 自己最常见）。对比 cnde-yilin r150：12.9% CNDE active——同样稀疏。31 runs × 2450 CNDE-control ticks ≈ 76k effective UB#4 tests，没出 → 真实率 <0.001%/tick 或需要 specific traffic（AV 前方 dense BV cluster + lane change 同时发生）。

this_week: Drafted and finalized the Q2 data requirements package for Isuzu, covering three categories: HD Maps (§1), Driving Trajectory Data for SMART Model Adaptation (§2), and Multimodal Sensor Data for the Sensor Reconstruction Pipeline (§3).
Defined the full per-clip data schema for SMART training (agents.json, map.json, traffic_lights.json, manifest.json) and published the Inchor SMART Driving Data Contract v0.1 as a companion document.

Refined Section 2 based on team review: removed Waymo TFRecords dependency, replaced with explicit field schema; increased data volume minimums; added labeling and precision requirements; clarified traffic signal format (Time Phase Diagram preferred); updated map coverage buffer to 500 m–1 km.
Prepared client-facing email to Isuzu with all three attached specification documents.

Designed a 3-stage adversity integration plan for the NCRC co-sim and completed Stage 1 (TeraSim/SUMO only, no Autoware, no CNDE): created ncrc_adversity_stage1.yaml, aa_stage1.sumocfg, and ncrc_stage1_bvs.rou.xml with hand-crafted BV placement calibrated to the AV's actual post-warmup position. Key discovery: all NCRC edges are highway.secondary (17.88 m/s < 25 m/s threshold), so get_location() returns intersection — adversity location filter must be intersection, not highway. Verified: 52 cutin + 19 rearend adversity fires per 600 s run, consistent across 8+ runs via scripts/verify_ncrc_stage1.sh.
next_week: Send the Q2 data requirements package to Isuzu and await feedback.

Stage 3: Integrate Autoware into the co-sim and validate full-stack adversity triggering during live AV navigation.
